the canonical neutrino transition probability is the result of an exact cancellation of two terms in the cross section, one of which is the interference of the neutrino and antineutrino source process, and the other is the interference of neutrino and antiparticle source and detection processes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

neutrino oscillations can be understood as the interference of two different paths of a neutrino mass eigenstate, one path going through the source and detector processes, the other one going only through the detector process.

the neutrino transition probability is a cross section for the combined source-detection process and that the canonical neutrino transition formula is the leading term of this cross section in the weak coupling regime.
the canonical neutrino formula, which is derived in the framework of a quantum-mechanical two-level system, is the cross section for the neutrino oscillation process in the field-theoretic approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neutrino state oscillating in vacuum is a coherent superposition of neutrino mass eigenstates, which is a consequence of the canonical oscillation formula and the field-theoretical treatment of neutrino oscillation.

the neutrino oscillation probability is not the probability for a neutrino to be in a certain mass eigenstate but rather it is the probability for a mass eigenstate to be detected as a neutrino with definite flavour.
neutrino oscillations are a genuine quantum phenomenon, which cannot be understood in terms of a classical wave propagation.
